title: promote-latest --rollback refuses a prior newer than the release (paired with quest-cli, Article 3)
description: Found by the LCLI-613 implementer while matching quest-cli QCLI-390 rules exactly (2026-09-27). Both repos --rollback checks accept a hand-edited record whose priorLatest is NEWER than the release, e.g. priorLatest "5.7.0" in a 5.6.7 record. It passes "strict X.Y.Z and differs from record.version" and "current latest is record.version or its prior" while latest still reads 5.6.7, so --rollback (not gated on a pair receipt, by design) moves latest onto an unqualified version. Fix in BOTH repos at once so the verdicts stay identical: require every priorLatest to be semver-LESS than record.version. lore implemented this once and removed it to keep parity with quest; re-add it here together with quest-cli.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore promote-latest --rollback refuses any priorLatest that is not semver-less than record.version, proven by a test with a newer prior
quest-cli mirrors the same rule, cited with both SHAs
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

plan: 1. Read quest-cli QCLI-391 by ref (opum-ai/quest-cli#353 head 83291e2d) for validateRecord + compareReleaseVersions.

2. scripts/promote-latest.mjs: add exported compareReleaseVersions beside RELEASE_VERSION (per component: length, then lexical); in validateRecord refuse a non-X.Y.Z record.version with no comparison (R1) and, as an else-if after the existing prior checks, a priorLatest newer than record.version (R2).

4. New test/lcli617-prior-latest-less-than.test.ts: greater/equal/lesser, numeric-not-lexical both ways, a component past 2^53, malformed record.version, and an end-to-end --rollback via main() with a newer prior plus a positive control.
5. Mutation control: remove R2, remove R1, make R3 lexical; predict and record the red subset each time.
6. Gates: bun test, typecheck, lint, bun run lore check; PR to dev with the verdict-equivalence table; tracker note.
implementationNotes: Paired with quest-cli QCLI-391 (record via opum-ai/quest-cli#317), agreed 2026-09-27, landing after the 0.11.0 pair ships. The rule: every priorLatest must compare semver-LESS than record.version, NUMERICALLY per component, so 0.10.0 > 0.9.0. The tests must include that numeric-not-lexical case, since a string comparison gets it backwards.

Implemented R1/R2/R3 (paired with quest-cli QCLI-391, read BY REF: opum-ai/quest-cli#353 head 83291e2d205c03ac22dca408fb237fafe7c8838d, scripts/promote-release.mjs lines 186-259). compareReleaseVersions is exported beside RELEASE_VERSION (per component: length, then lexical). validateRecord refuses a record.version that is not a plain X.Y.Z (one problem, no comparison), and as an else-if after the existing prior checks refuses a prior newer than record.version. Launcher: priors are compared against record.version, never launcherVersion; validateRecord never reads launcherVersion, and the launcher's prior is its own pre-promotion latest, already held to X.Y.Z, so nothing changes for it.

PR opum-ai/lore-cli#354 (head aa88f405 at the time of this note). quest-cli ref read BY REF: opum-ai/quest-cli#353 head 83291e2d205c03ac22dca408fb237fafe7c8838d (OPEN when read), scripts/promote-release.mjs validateRecord + compareReleaseVersions, lines 186-259. VERDICT EQUIVALENCE, measured by running those lines verbatim beside lore's validateRecord: 50 inputs read of 50 expected, each on the --rollback path (no {version}) and the resume path ({version: 9.9.9}); compareReleaseVersions 121 pairs, 0 sign differences. Same verdict on: priors 9.10.0 / 10.0.0 / 9.9.10 in a 9.9.9 record (refuse), 5.7.0 in 5.6.7 (refuse), equal (refuse), 9.9.8 in 9.9.9 (accept), 9.9.9 in 9.10.0 (accept), 0.10.0 in 0.9.0 (refuse), 0.9.0 in 0.10.0 (accept), 0.0.9007199254740993 in 0.0.9007199254740992 (refuse) and the reverse (accept), record.version latest / v9.9.9 / 9.9.9-rc.1 / undefined / null / 999 / 09.9.9 / trailing newline (refuse), and prior number / latest / 09.9.8 (refuse). ONE DIVERGENCE (4 of the 50 inputs): record.version as a JSON array ["9.9.9"]. lore refuses it with an R1 problem; quest's STRICT_SEMVER.test coerces it to a match, then compareReleaseVersions throws TypeError (b.split is not a function). Nothing moves in either repo, but quest crashes out of main where lore exits 1. Recommend quest adds the typeof guard. MUTATION CONTROL, with the red subset predicted before each run: M1 remove R2, 7 red / 16 green; M2 remove R1, 6 red / 17 green; M3 lexical R3, 8 red / 15 green; M4 Number() R3, 2 red / 21 green. Every result matched its prediction exactly. PREMISE FINDING, the same in both repos: neither planPromotion refuses an older --version, so a backport promoted over a newer latest (0.10.5 over 0.11.0, measured) writes a record that this rule refuses on resume and on --rollback. That is outside this task's file scope, so it needs a decision on whether planPromotion should refuse up front.
